missionObjectives.title: The Hidden Threat in Earth Orbit
missionObjectives.description: Earth's orbit is crowded — with over 100 million pieces of debris traveling at extreme speeds. These fragments, often smaller than a marble, can cause catastrophic damage to active satellites.
missionObjectives.subDescription: While most detection systems only identify debris larger than 3-5cm, TejoOne aims to push this boundary by using a compact, affordable platform. Our mission: to help build a public debris catalog and make orbit cleaner and safer.

association.title: Espaço ao Cubo
association.subtitle: Youth association dedicated to technology development and promoting education in the space sector
association.intro1: We are a passionate group of students united by the dream of reaching space. Our team brings together engineering students from various disciplines, physicists, designers and legal scholars who work collaboratively to develop the first Portuguese CubeSat for space debris detection, designed and built entirely by students.
association.intro2: Beyond the technical challenge, we believe in the power of education and inspiration. We conduct workshops and educational activities from primary to higher education. We also participate in events and lectures, sharing our passion for space with the community, showing that the sky is not the limit.

subsystems.title: Subsystems
subsystems.subtitle: TejoOne consists of several subsystems working together to ensure mission success

obdh.name: OBDH
obdh.details: O computador de bordo é responsável pelo processamento de dados e controlo geral do satélite. Gere as operações dos subsistemas, armazena telemetria e executa comandos recebidos da estação terrestre.
obdh.description: On-board computer responsible for data processing and general satellite control.
obdh.specs: Processor: ARM Cortex-M4, Memory: 256KB Flash, 64KB RAM, Interfaces: I2C, SPI, UART

comms.name: COMMS
comms.details: The communications system enables data exchange between the satellite and the ground station. It uses UHF/VHF bands to transmit telemetry and receive commands, ensuring a reliable link throughout the mission.
comms.description: Radio communications system for sending telemetry and receiving commands.
comms.specs: Band: UHF/VHF, Frequency: 437 MHz (TX), 145 MHz (RX), Data Rate: 1200 bps

eps.name: EPS
eps.details: The EPS manages the generation, storage, and distribution of electrical power on the satellite. It uses solar panels to capture energy from the sun and batteries to store it, ensuring all subsystems have sufficient power to operate.
eps.description: Power system with solar panels and batteries for satellite power supply.
eps.specs: Solar Panels: 4 × GaAs, Battery: Li-ion 5.2Wh, Voltage: 3.7V

adcs.name: ADCS
adcs.details: The ADCS is responsible for determining and controlling the satellite's attitude in orbit. It uses sensors like magnetometers and gyroscopes to measure orientation, and actuators like reaction wheels and magnetorquers to adjust position as needed.
adcs.description: Attitude determination and control system for satellite orientation.
adcs.specs: Sensors: Magnetometers, Gyroscopes, Actuators: Reaction wheels, Magnetorquers

payload.name: Payload
payload.details: The TejoOne payload is a camera designed to capture images of Earth and space. With a resolution of 640 × 480 pixels and a field of view of 60°, the camera stores images on a 2GB memory card for later analysis.
payload.description: Camera for capturing images of Earth and space.
payload.specs: Resolution: 640 × 480 pixels, Field of View: 60°, Storage: 2GB

structure.name: Structure
structure.details: The TejoOne structure is a 1U mechanical platform compatible with the CubeSat standard. Made from Aluminum 6061-T6, the structure provides physical support and protection to the internal subsystems, ensuring satellite integrity during launch and operation in orbit.
structure.description: 1U mechanical structure compatible with CubeSat standard.

thermal.name: Thermal
thermal.details: The TejoOne thermal system maintains the operational temperature of the subsystems within safe limits. It uses passive thermal control methods, such as coatings and insulation, to protect sensitive components from extreme temperature variations in the space environment.
thermal.description: Thermal control system to maintain operational temperature.
thermal.specs: Operating Range: -10°C to +50°C, Survival Range: -20°C to +60°C, Control: Passive
